attributes.doc: Sets the attributes of a sector.

altitude.doc: The elevation of the sector, in meters.

approach.doc: The approach time to the sector, in minutes.

children.doc: Indicates whether the sector is suitable for children.

driesafterrain.doc: How long the sector takes to dry after rain.

orientation.doc: Possible values: n, ne, e, se, s, sw, w, nw.

rock.doc: Possible values: granite, limestone, sandstone, quartzite.

sun.doc: The time of day when the sector is in the sun.

background.doc: Sets the background image for the current section.

geolocation.doc: Defines the geolocation of the current section. The location appears on the geomap and is marked active when the section heading is prominent.

coords.doc: A latitude and longitude pair such as 42.0931, 19.1002.

direction.doc: The position of the title relative to the marker. Valid values are nw (north west), n (north), ne (north east), e (east), se (south east), s (south), sw (south west), and w (west).

marker.doc: The name of a marker in Climbers-Heaven.kml. The marker must be in the folder specified by the preceding geomap directive.

show-title.doc: The first zoom level at which the marker title is shown on the map. Use no if the title should never be shown.

geomap.doc: Shows a map in the overview section and displays the geolocations collected from the current section and its subsections.

folder.doc: The name of a folder in Climbers-Heaven.kml. The geomap shows all visible objects defined in that folder.

levels.doc: Controls how deeply geolocations are collected. A value of 0 includes only the current section. A value of 1 also includes the subsections, and so on.

imagelist.doc: Displays the given images. If an XMP comment is set in the image metadata, the comment is shown as the image subtitle.

created.doc: The year the route was created.

first-ascent.doc: The climber or team that made the first ascent.

other.doc: Possible values: dangerous, partly bolted, runout.

stars.doc: The route quality from 0 to 4 stars.

steepness.doc: Possible values: slab, vertical, overhang, roof.

style.doc: Possible values: fingery, powerful, dyno, tufa, pockets, crack, endurance, technical, mental, crag.

topo-id.doc: The ID used in the topo SVG. This option is usually not needed because the route is linked to the topo by name. Use it only when the route name is not unique, such as Open Project.

routestatistics.doc: Shows a bar chart of the grades of the routes described in the following sections.

levels.doc: Controls how deeply routes are collected for the statistics. A value of 0 includes only the current section. A value of 1 also includes the subsections, and so on.

summary.doc: Controls where the total number of routes appears in the chart. e (east) places it on the right side, and w (west) places it on the left side.

topo.doc: Defines an SVG topo for the current section.
